items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy 'what if' geography Short for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is SUPER excited and happy, practically bursting with energy: a hyped-up, thrilled YouTube host who can't wait to reveal a hilarious true story. Huge smile in the voice the whole way, bright, punchy and lively. 'Here's the twist... they're already halfway there!' is a big grinning reveal. '...and accidentally invaded Liechtenstein!' is delighted, barely holding back a laugh. 'Nobody there even noticed.' is a deadpan comic beat. 'But that's not even the weirdest part' is leaned-in and conspiratorial, at a normal pace, not rushed. 'And the story goes... eighty-one came back!' is a big amazed punchline. In the next-to-last line, Switzerland's words are calm and confident, and Liechtenstein's words are a small, nervous voice. The last line trails off unfinished, voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Keep the dramatic pauses on the '...' marks short and punchy, never long. Never slow, flat, calm, sleepy or documentary-serious, and never rushed. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same high energy throughout. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. Pronounce Liechtenstein as LIK-ten-shtine, Vaduz as fah-DOOTS, Bern as BERN, Swiss franc as SWISS FRANK.
lines: What if Switzerland and Liechtenstein became one country?
Switzerland is two hundred sixty times bigger. Liechtenstein is just twenty-five kilometres long.
And it has no army. Zero.
Here's the twist... they're already halfway there!
Same money: the Swiss franc, since nineteen twenty-four.
Swiss customs officers even guard Liechtenstein's border!
In two thousand seven, a hundred and seventy Swiss soldiers got lost at night...
But that's not even the weirdest part.
In eighteen sixty-six, its last army marched off to war... with eighty men.
And the story goes... eighty-one came back!
And the capital? Bern? Or tiny Vaduz?
Switzerland: Relax, we'll protect you. Liechtenstein: Just... don't get lost again.
So... one country, or two? Because honestly...
